verses.zh: 扫罗家和大卫家争战许久。大卫家日见强盛；扫罗家日见衰弱。
verses.en: However, the war was prolonged between the house of Saul and the house of David. David was becoming steadily stronger, while the house of Saul was becoming increasingly weaker.

verses.zh: 大卫在希伯仑得了几个儿子：长子暗嫩是耶斯列人亚希暖所生的；
verses.en: Now sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, born to Ahinoam the Jezreelite.

verses.zh: 次子基利押（在历代上三章一节作但以利）是作过迦密人拿八的妻亚比该所生的；三子押沙龙是基述王达买的女儿玛迦所生的；
verses.en: His second son[NOTE:1] was Kileab, born to Abigail the widow[NOTE:2] of Nabal the Carmelite. His third son was Absalom, the son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur.
notes: The Hebrew text does not have the word “son.” So also in vv. 3-5.
Heb “wife.”

verses.zh: 四子亚多尼雅是哈及所生的；五子示法提雅是亚比她所生的；
verses.en: His fourth son was Adonijah, the son of Haggith. His fifth son was Shephatiah, the son of Abital.

verses.zh: 六子以特念是大卫的妻以格拉所生的。大卫这六个儿子都是在希伯仑生的。
verses.en: His sixth son was Ithream, born to David’s wife Eglah. These sons[NOTE:1] were all born to David in Hebron.
notes: The Hebrew text does not have “sons.”

verses.zh: 扫罗家和大卫家争战的时候，押尼珥在扫罗家大有权势。
verses.en: As the war continued between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner was becoming more influential[NOTE:1] in the house of Saul.
notes: Heb “was strengthening himself.” The statement may have a negative sense here, perhaps suggesting that Abner was overstepping the bounds of political propriety in a self-serving way.

verses.zh: 扫罗有一妃嫔，名叫利斯巴，是爱亚的女儿。一日，伊施波设对押尼珥说：「你为甚么与我父的妃嫔同房呢？」
verses.en: Now Saul had a concubine named Rizpah daughter of Aiah. Ish Bosheth[NOTE:1] said to Abner, “Why did you sleep with[NOTE:2] my father’s concubine?”[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew of the MT reads simply “and he said,” with no expressed subject for the verb. It is not likely that the text originally had no expressed subject for this verb, since the antecedent is not immediately clear from the context. We should probably restore to the Hebrew text the name “Ish Bosheth.” See a few medieval Hebrew mss, Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotion, and Vulgate. Perhaps the name was accidentally omitted by homoioarcton. Note that both the name Ish Bosheth and the following preposition אֶל (ʾel) begin with the letter alef.
The expression בּוֹא אֶל (boʾ ʾel) means “come to” or “approach,” but is also used as a euphemism for sexual relations.

This accusation against Abner is a very serious one, since an act of sexual infringement on the king’s harem would probably have been understood as a blatant declaration of aspirations to kingship. As such it was not merely a matter of ethical impropriety but an act of grave political significance as well.

verses.zh: 押尼珥因伊施波设的话就甚发怒，说：「我岂是犹大的狗头呢？我恩待你父扫罗的家和他的弟兄、朋友，不将你交在大卫手里，今日你竟为这妇人责备我吗？
verses.en: These words of Ish Bosheth really angered Abner and he said, “Am I the head of a dog that belongs to Judah? This very day I am demonstrating[NOTE:1] loyalty to the house of Saul your father and to his relatives[NOTE:2] and his friends! I have not betrayed you into the hand of David. Yet you have accused me of sinning with this woman today![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “I do.”
Heb “brothers.”
Heb “and you have laid upon me the guilt of the woman today.”

verses.zh: 我若不照着耶和华起誓应许大卫的话行，废去扫罗的位，建立大卫的位，使他治理以色列和犹大，从但直到别是巴，愿　神重重地降罚与我！」
verses.en: God will severely judge Abner[NOTE:1] if I do not do for David exactly what the Lord has promised him,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “So will God do to Abner and so he will add to him.”
Heb “has sworn to David.” The LXX, with the exception of the recension of Origen, adds “in this day.”

verses.zh: a
verses.en: namely, to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul and to establish the throne of David over Israel and over Judah all the way from Dan to Beer Sheba!”

verses.zh: 伊施波设惧怕押尼珥，不敢回答一句。
verses.en: Ish Bosheth[NOTE:1] was unable to answer Abner with even a single word because he was afraid of him.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Ish Bosheth) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 押尼珥打发人去见大卫，替他说：「这国归谁呢？」又说：「你与我立约，我必帮助你，使以色列人都归服你。」
verses.en: Then Abner sent messengers[NOTE:1] to David saying, “To whom does the land belong? Make an agreement[NOTE:2] with me, and I will do whatever I can[NOTE:3] to cause all Israel to turn to you.”
notes: The Hebrew text adds here, “on his behalf.”
Heb “cut a covenant.” So also in vv. 13, 21.
Heb “and behold, my hand is with you.”

verses.zh: 大卫说：「好！我与你立约。但有一件，你来见我面的时候，若不将扫罗的女儿米甲带来，必不得见我的面。」
verses.en: So David said, “Good! I will make an agreement with you. I ask only one thing from you. You will not see my face unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal when you come to visit me.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The words “when you come to see my face,” though found in the Hebrew text, are somewhat redundant given the similar expression in the earlier part of the verse. The words are absent from the Syriac Peshitta.

verses.zh: 大卫就打发人去见扫罗的儿子伊施波设，说：「你要将我的妻米甲归还我；她是我从前用一百非利士人的阳皮所聘定的。」
verses.en: David sent messengers to Ish Bosheth son of Saul with this demand:[NOTE:1] “Give me my wife Michal whom I acquired[NOTE:2] for 100 Philistine foreskins.”
notes: Heb “to Ish Bosheth son of Saul saying.” To avoid excessive sibilance (especially when read aloud) the translation renders “saying” as “with this demand.”
Heb “whom I betrothed to myself.”

verses.zh: 伊施波设就打发人去，将米甲从拉亿的儿子、她丈夫帕铁那里接回来。
verses.en: So Ish Bosheth took her[NOTE:1] from her husband Paltiel[NOTE:2] son of Laish.
notes: Heb “sent and took her.”
Heb “Go, return.”

verses.zh: 米甲的丈夫跟着她，一面走一面哭，直跟到巴户琳。押尼珥说：「你回去吧！」帕铁就回去了。
verses.en: Her husband went along behind her, weeping all the way to Bahurim. Finally Abner said to him, “Go back!”[NOTE:1] So he returned home.
notes: Heb “the word of Abner was with.”

verses.zh: 押尼珥对以色列长老说：「从前你们愿意大卫作王治理你们，
verses.en: Abner advised[NOTE:1] the elders of Israel, “Previously you were wanting David to be your king.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you were seeking David to be king over you.”

The present translation follows the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate in reading “I will save,” rather than the MT “he saved” or “to save." The context calls for the first person common singular imperfect of the verb rather than the third person masculine singular perfect or the infinitive construct.

verses.zh: 现在你们可以照心愿而行。因为耶和华曾论到大卫说：『我必藉我仆人大卫的手，救我民以色列脱离非利士人和众仇敌的手。』」
verses.en: Act now! For the Lord has said to David, ‘By the hand of my servant David I will save[NOTE:1] my people Israel from[NOTE:2] the Philistines and from all their enemies.’”
notes: Heb “from the hand of.”
Heb “into the ears of.”

verses.zh: 押尼珥也用这话说给便雅悯人听，又到希伯仑，将以色列人和便雅悯全家一切所喜悦的事说给大卫听。
verses.en: Then Abner spoke privately with[NOTE:1] the Benjaminites. Abner also went to Hebron to inform David privately[NOTE:2] of all that Israel and the entire house of Benjamin had agreed to.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “also Abner went to speak into the ears of David in Hebron.”
Heb “all which was good in the eyes of Israel and in the eyes of all the house of Benjamin.”
After the cohortatives, the prefixed verbal form with the prefixed conjunction indicates purpose or result.

verses.zh: 押尼珥带着二十个人来到希伯仑见大卫，大卫就为押尼珥和他带来的人设摆筵席。
verses.en: When Abner, accompanied by 20 men, came to David in Hebron, David prepared a banquet for Abner and the men who were with him.

verses.zh: 押尼珥对大卫说：「我要起身去招聚以色列众人来见我主我王，与你立约，你就可以照着心愿作王。」于是大卫送押尼珥去，押尼珥就平平安安地去了。
verses.en: Abner said to David, “Let me leave so that I may go and gather all Israel to my lord the king so that they may make an agreement[NOTE:1] with you. Then you will rule over all that you desire.” So David sent Abner away, and he left in peace.
notes: Heb “And look, the servants of David.”

verses.zh: 约押和大卫的仆人攻击敌军，带回许多的掠物。那时押尼珥不在希伯仑大卫那里，因大卫已经送他去，他也平平安安地去了。
verses.en: Now David’s soldiers[NOTE:1] and Joab were coming back from a raid, bringing a great deal of plunder with them. Abner was no longer with David in Hebron, for David[NOTE:2] had sent him away and he had left in peace.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “Look, Abner.”

verses.zh: 约押和跟随他的全军到了，就有人告诉约押说：「尼珥的儿子押尼珥来见王，王送他去，他也平平安安地去了。」
verses.en: When Joab and all the army that was with him arrived, Joab was told: “Abner the son of Ner came to the king; he sent him away, and he left in peace!”

verses.zh: 约押去见王说：「你这是做甚么呢？押尼珥来见你，你为何送他去，他就踪影不见了呢？
verses.en: So Joab went to the king and said, “What have you done? Abner[NOTE:1] has come to you. Why would you send him away? Now he’s gone on his way![NOTE:2]
notes: The LXX adds “in peace.”

Heb “your going out and your coming in.” The expression is a merism. It specifically mentions the polar extremities of the actions but includes all activity in between the extremities as well, thus encompassing the entirety of one’s activities.

verses.zh: 你当晓得，尼珥的儿子押尼珥来是要诓哄你，要知道你的出入和你一切所行的事。」
verses.en: You know Abner the son of Ner. Surely he came here to spy on you and to determine when you leave and when you return[NOTE:1] and to discover everything that you are doing!”
notes: Heb “and he struck him down there [in] the stomach.”

verses.zh: 约押从大卫那里出来，就打发人去追赶押尼珥，在西拉井追上他，将他带回来，大卫却不知道。
verses.en: Then Joab left David and sent messengers after Abner. They brought him back from the well of Sirah. (But David was not aware of it.)

verses.zh: 押尼珥回到希伯仑，约押领他到城门的瓮洞，假作要与他说机密话，就在那里刺透他的肚腹，他便死了。这是报杀他兄弟亚撒黑的仇。
verses.en: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside at the gate as if to speak privately with him. Joab then stabbed him[NOTE:1] in the abdomen and killed him, avenging the shed blood of his brother Asahel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and he [i.e., Abner] died on account of the blood of Asahel his [i.e., Joab’s] brother.”

Heb “and may they whirl over.” In the Hebrew text the subject of the plural verb is unexpressed. The most likely subject is Abner’s “shed blood” (v. 28), which is a masculine plural form in Hebrew. The verb חוּל (khul, “whirl”) is used with the preposition עַל (ʿal) only here and in Jer 23:19; 30:23.

verses.zh: 大卫听见了，就说：「流尼珥的儿子押尼珥的血，这罪在耶和华面前必永不归我和我的国。
verses.en: When David later heard about this, he said, “I and my kingdom are forever innocent before the Lord of the shed blood of Abner son of Ner.

verses.zh: 愿流他血的罪归到约押头上和他父的全家；又愿约押家不断有患漏症的，长大麻疯的，架拐而行的，被刀杀死的，缺乏饮食的。」
verses.en: May his blood whirl over[NOTE:1] the head of Joab and the entire house of his father![NOTE:2] May the males of Joab’s house[NOTE:3] never cease to have[NOTE:4] someone with a running sore or a skin disease or one who works at the spindle[NOTE:5] or one who falls by the sword or one who lacks food!”
notes: 4QSama has “of Joab” rather than “of his father” read by the MT.

Heb “the house of Joab.” However, it is necessary to specify that David’s curse is aimed at Joab’s male descendants; otherwise it would not be clear that “one who works at the spindle” refers to a man doing woman’s work rather than a woman.
Heb “and may there not be cut off from the house of Joab.”

The expression used here is difficult. The translation “one who works at the spindle” follows a suggestion of S. R. Driver that the expression pejoratively describes an effeminate man who, rather than being a mighty warrior, is occupied with tasks that are normally fulfilled by women (S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 250-51; cf. NAB “one unmanly”; TEV “fit only to do a woman’s work”; CEV “cowards”). But P. K. McCarter, following an alleged Phoenician usage of the noun to refer to “crutches,” adopts a different view. He translates the phrase “clings to a crutch,” seeing here a further description of physical lameness (II Samuel [AB], 118). Such an idea fits the present context well and is followed by NIV, NCV, and NLT, although the evidence for this meaning is questionable. According to DNWSI 2:915-16, the noun consistently refers to a spindle in Phoenician, as it does in Ugaritic (see UT 468).
Heb “was walking.”

verses.zh: 约押和他兄弟亚比筛杀了押尼珥，是因押尼珥在基遍争战的时候杀了他们的兄弟亚撒黑。
verses.en: So Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel in Gibeon during the battle.

verses.zh: 大卫吩咐约押和跟随他的众人说：「你们当撕裂衣服，腰束麻布，在押尼珥棺前哀哭。」大卫王也跟在棺后。
verses.en: David instructed Joab and all the people who were with him, “Tear your clothes. Put on sackcloth. Lament before Abner!” Now King David followed[NOTE:1] behind the funeral pallet.[NOTE:2]
notes: A ‫מִטָּה‬ (mittah) is typically bed with a frame (which can be ornate and covered with blankets and pillows). Here, like a stretcher, it is a portable frame for carrying a body, technically a bier.
Heb “lifted up his voice and wept.” The expression is a verbal hendiadys.

verses.zh: 他们将押尼珥葬在希伯仑。王在押尼珥的墓旁放声而哭，众民也都哭了。
verses.en: So they buried Abner in Hebron. The king cried loudly[NOTE:1] over Abner’s grave, and all the people wept too.
notes: The translation follows many medieval Hebrew manuscripts and several ancient versions in reading “your hands,” rather than “your hand.”

verses.zh: 王为押尼珥举哀，说：押尼珥何竟像愚顽人死呢？
verses.en: The king chanted the following lament for Abner:“Should Abner have died like a fool?

verses.zh: 你手未曾捆绑，脚未曾锁住。你死，如人死在罪孽之辈手下一样。于是众民又为押尼珥哀哭。
verses.en: Your hands[NOTE:1] were not bound,and your feet were not put into irons.You fell the way one falls before criminals.”All the people[NOTE:2] wept over him again.
notes: 4QSama lacks the words “all the people.”
Heb “Thus God will do to me and thus he will add.”

verses.zh: 日头未落的时候，众民来劝大卫吃饭，但大卫起誓说：「我若在日头未落以前吃饭，或吃别物，愿　神重重地降罚与我！」
verses.en: Then all the people came and encouraged David to eat food while it was still day. But David took an oath saying, “God will punish me severely[NOTE:1] if I taste bread or anything whatsoever before the sun sets!”
notes: Heb “it was good in their eyes.”

verses.zh: 众民知道了就都喜悦。凡王所行的，众民无不喜悦。
verses.en: All the people noticed this and it pleased them.[NOTE:1] In fact, everything the king did pleased all the people.
notes: Heb “from the king.”

verses.zh: 那日，以色列众民才知道杀尼珥的儿子押尼珥并非出于王意。
verses.en: All the people and all Israel realized on that day that the killing of Abner son of Ner was not done at the king’s instigation.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “a leader and a great one.” The expression is a hendiadys.

verses.zh: 王对臣仆说：「你们岂不知今日以色列人中死了一个作元帅的大丈夫吗？
verses.en: Then the king said to his servants, “Do you not realize that a great leader[NOTE:1] has fallen this day in Israel?
notes: Heb “are hard from me.”

verses.zh: 我虽然受膏为王，今日还是软弱；这洗鲁雅的两个儿子比我刚强。愿耶和华照着恶人所行的恶报应他。」
verses.en: Today I am weak, even though I am anointed as king. These men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too much for me to bear![NOTE:1] May the Lord punish appropriately the one who has done this evil thing!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “May the Lord repay the doer of the evil according to his evil” (NASB similar).
